text: First principle: any explanation is better than none at all.
location: The Four Great Errors 5
plain: We grab the first comforting answer just to stop feeling uneasy, and call it truth.

text: To trace something unfamiliar back to something familiar, is at once a relief, a comfort and a satisfaction, while it also produces a feeling of power.
location: The Four Great Errors 5
plain: Naming a strange thing makes you feel safe and in control, whether or not you understood it.

text: The banker thinks immediately of business, the Christian of “sin,” and the girl of her love affair.
location: The Four Great Errors 5
plain: Everyone explains the world through whatever already fills their head.

text: No one is responsible for the fact that he exists at all, that he is constituted as he is, and that he happens to be in certain circumstances and in a particular environment.
location: The Four Great Errors 8
plain: You did not pick your start. Stop judging yourself for the hand you were dealt.

text: The individual in his past and future is a piece of fate, one law the more, one necessity the more for all that is to come and is to be.
location: Morality as the Enemy of Nature 6
plain: You are part of how things had to go. You belong here.

text: We do not deny readily, we glory in saying yea to things.
location: Morality as the Enemy of Nature 6
plain: Say yes to life first and push back second.

text: One must not respond immediately to a stimulus; one must acquire a command of the obstructing and isolating instincts.
location: Things the Germans Lack 6
plain: Do not react the second something hits you. Learn to hold the pause.

text: All lack of intellectuality, all vulgarity, arises out of the inability to resist a stimulus:—one must respond or react, every impulse is indulged.
location: Things the Germans Lack 6
plain: Cheap behavior is just not being able to say no to the urge in front of you.

text: After all, nobody can spend more than he has:—this is true of individuals, it is also true of nations.
location: Things the Germans Lack 4
plain: Your energy and attention are a budget. Spend them in one place and they are gone from the others.

text: To yearn for a strong faith is not the proof of a strong faith, but rather the reverse.
location: Skirmishes in a War with the Age 12
plain: Craving certainty means you do not have it.

text: If a man have a strong faith he can indulge in the luxury of scepticism; he is strong enough, firm enough, well-knit enough for such a luxury.
location: Skirmishes in a War with the Age 12
plain: Only the secure can afford to doubt freely.

text: In order to acquire intellect, one must be in need of it.
location: Skirmishes in a War with the Age 14
plain: You get sharp when you have to. Pressure builds the mind.

text: In the midst of an experience a man should not turn his eyes upon himself; in such cases any eye becomes the “evil eye.”
location: Skirmishes in a War with the Age 7
plain: Stop watching yourself live. Be in the thing.

text: One must know who one is.
location: Skirmishes in a War with the Age 7
plain: Know who you are before anything else.

text: To experience things on purpose—this is not a bit of good.
location: Skirmishes in a War with the Age 7
plain: Forced, staged experience is worthless. Live it for real.

text: The most intellectual men, provided they are also the most courageous, experience the most excruciating tragedies: but on that very account they honour life, because it confronts them with its most formidable antagonism.
location: Skirmishes in a War with the Age 17
plain: The braver and smarter you are, the harder life hits you, and you love it for giving you something worth fighting.

text: A courageous and free spirit, in the presence of a mighty foe, in the presence of a sublime misfortune, and face to face with a problem that inspires horror—this is the triumphant attitude which the tragic artist selects and which he glorifies.
location: Skirmishes in a War with the Age 24
plain: Facing the terrible thing without flinching is the winning posture.

text: Those things for which we find words, are things wehave already overcome.
location: Skirmishes in a War with the Age 26
plain: If you can talk about it easily, you are already past it.

text: In all speech there lies an element of contempt.
location: Skirmishes in a War with the Age 26
plain: Talking cheapens what you felt.

text: The means with which Julius Cæsar preserved himself against sickness and headaches: heavy marches, the simplest mode of living, uninterrupted sojourns in the open air, continual hardships,—generally speaking these are the self-preservative and self-defensive measures against the extreme vulnerability of those subtle machines working at the highest pressure, which are called geniuses.
location: Skirmishes in a War with the Age 31
plain: High performers stay sane through hard physical work, simple living, and fresh air.

text: That which justifies man is his reality,—it will justify him to all eternity.
location: Skirmishes in a War with the Age 32
plain: What you actually do is what counts, not what you wish.

text: There is a small dose of revenge in every lamentation.
location: Skirmishes in a War with the Age 34
plain: Every complaint is a bit of payback in disguise.

text: One never perishes through anybody’s fault but one’s own.
location: Skirmishes in a War with the Age 36
plain: Nobody ruins you but you.

text: Sometimes the value of a thing does not lie in that which it helps us to achieve, but in the amount we have to pay for it,—what it costs us.
location: Skirmishes in a War with the Age 38
plain: Things are worth what you pay to get them.

text: Freedom is the will to be responsible for ourselves. It is to preserve the distance which separates us from other men. To grow more indifferent to hardship, to severity, to privation, and even to life itself.
location: Skirmishes in a War with the Age 38
plain: Freedom means owning your life, keeping your distance from the crowd, and not caring about hardship.

text: First principle: a man must need to be strong, otherwise he will never attain it.
location: Skirmishes in a War with the Age 38
plain: You only get strong if you need to be.

text: The genius—in work and in deed,—is necessarily a squanderer: the fact that he spends himself constitutes his greatness.
location: Skirmishes in a War with the Age 44
plain: Greatness means burning yourself out on the work without hedging.

text: The first rule of all:—nobody must “let himself go,” not even when he is alone.
location: Skirmishes in a War with the Age 47
plain: Hold your standard when nobody is watching.

text: Everything good is an inheritance: that which is not inherited is imperfect, it is simply a beginning.
location: Skirmishes in a War with the Age 47
plain: Anything you build alone is just a start. Greatness stacks over generations.

text: The aphorism, the sentence, in both of which I, as the first among Germans, am a master, are the forms of “eternity”; it is my ambition to say in ten sentences what everyone else says in a whole book,—what everyone else does not say in a whole book.
location: Skirmishes in a War with the Age 51
plain: Say in ten lines what others cannot say in a book.

text: The formula of our happiness: a Yea, a Nay, a straight line, a goal.
location: Section 1
plain: Happiness is a yes, a no, a straight line, and a target.

text: What is good? All that enhances the feeling of power, the Will to Power, and power itself in man.
location: Section 2
plain: Good is whatever makes you stronger.

text: What is bad?—All that proceeds from weakness. What is happiness?—The feeling that power is increasing,—that resistance has been overcome.
location: Section 2
plain: Happiness is feeling yourself grow stronger by beating what resisted you.

text: Not contentment, but more power; not peace at any price, but war; not virtue, but efficiency (virtue in the Renaissance sense, virtu, free from all moralic acid).
location: Section 2
plain: Aim for strength over comfort, and fight over easy peace.

text: I call an animal, a species, an individual corrupt, when it loses its instincts, when it selects and prefers that which is detrimental to it.
location: Section 6
plain: You are in trouble when you start choosing what hurts you.

text: Life itself, to my mind, is nothing more nor less than the instinct of growth, of permanence, of accumulating forces, of power: where the will to power is lacking, degeneration sets in.
location: Section 6
plain: Life is growth. When you stop pushing to grow, you start to decay.

text: A man loses power when he pities.
location: Section 7
plain: Pity drains strength from both people.

text: A virtue must be our invention, our most personal defence and need: in every other sense it is merely a danger.
location: Section 11
plain: Build values out of your own needs, not borrowed rules.

text: What is there that destroys a man more speedily than to work, think, feel, as an automaton of “duty,” without internal promptings, without a profound personal predilection, without joy?
location: Section 11
plain: Nothing kills you faster than grinding through duty with no joy of your own in it.

text: The most valuable standpoints are always the last to be found: but the most valuable standpoints are the methods.
location: Section 13
plain: The best insights come last, and the best of them are about how to work.

text: The pathos which grows out of this state, is called Faith: that is to say, to shut one’s eyes once and for all, in order not to suffer at the sight of incurable falsity.
location: Section 9
plain: Faith can be closing your eyes so you do not have to see what hurts.

text: What is the only kind of man who has reasons for wriggling out of reality by lies? The man who suffers from reality.
location: Section 15
plain: People lie to themselves when reality hurts them.

text: When a man is in love he endures more than at other times; he submits to everything.
location: Section 23
plain: Love makes you put up with almost anything.

text: We deny that anything can be done perfectly so long as it is done consciously.
location: Section 14
plain: Your best work comes when you stop overthinking it.
